overview: This 447-page file traces U.S. and Allied decisions about Japanese merchant shipping from occupation through 1949. It covers captured-vessel restitution, reparations, fleet and shipbuilding limits, private operation, overseas trade, port access, and fishing-vessel seizures. Policy papers, diplomatic correspondence, shipping-industry protests, operational directives, and Japan’s Mariners Law reveal competing economic, security, and commercial priorities.
interest: The file brings policy debates, industry objections, crew reports, and operating rules together, showing how occupation controls shaped Japan’s maritime recovery.
